Report concrete timestamps.

Identify everything that changed around the symptom window across ALL services, not only order-service. Use get_deployments and get_config_changes for 2026-05-04 through 2026-05-05 to list deployments, config changes, and specifically the ledger-db autovacuum setting change (exact time, exact parameters, affected tables). Also use get_service_dependencies for order-service to map what it calls (does it call ledger-db directly, or via ledger-service?) and which services share ledger-db. Search historical incidents for prior autovacuum-change or ledger-db timeout incidents.

events.statement: The only config change in the 2026-05-04..2026-05-05 window is cfg-2903 on ledger-db: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor changed from 0.2 to 0.1 at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z by author 'dba-team', described as 'More aggressive autovacuum'. No affected-tables list was returned for this change.

The only deployment across ALL services in the window is dep-5905: portfolio-service v4.5.0 deployed 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z by k.shah, adding 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at', 'no migration included', status 'live', rolled_back_at null — i.e. NOT rolled back as of current data.

order-service connects DIRECTLY to ledger-db (edge order-service -> ledger-db, kind 'db'); there is no ledger-service in the dependency graph. Its other calls are pricing-engine and exchange-gateway (http) and kafka (queue-produce); api-gateway calls order-service.

ledger-db is shared=true and is used by four services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service (all 'db' edges into ledger-db). So any ledger-db contention can affect callers beyond order-service.

Ledger-db is also shared via redis-cache and kafka (both shared=true) in order-service's graph; pricing-engine reads redis-cache and market-data-service, so shared-component contention could enter via pricing-engine too.

History leads (not evidence for this incident): HIST-110 (2026-01-15) 'Slow orders from ledger-db IOPS throttling' with order-service+ledger-db and symptoms 'order latency','statement timeouts' (root_cause IOPS throttling); HIST-111 (2025-05-22) 'Reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db' (ledger-db+settlement-service, bad_deployment); HIST-102 portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover.

events.statement: order-service p99 latency was flat at ~143-166 ms through 08:52Z, then inflected at the 08:56Z bucket to avg 1514.78 ms / max 5607.8 ms and stepped up to ~5.2 s from 09:00Z onward. The 240-second bucket means the true crossing falls inside 08:52-08:56Z.

First order-service ERROR log is at 09:00:42Z; the only pattern is statement timeout against ledger-db: 'ledger-db: canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)'. 284 such errors were found in 08:00-10:59Z (order-service ERROR count = 284), i.e. roughly 1.5/min sustained, last seen 10:58:29Z.

ledger-db slow queries start EARLIER than the order-service symptom: first WARN at 08:58:38Z, and every slow-query log line is 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' with application_name=portfolio-service - none are attributed to order-service.

portfolio-service shows the earliest and largest latency degradation: p99 flat at ~173-194 ms through 08:52Z, then 08:56Z bucket avg 3574.3 ms / max 7056.7 ms, rising to ~6.7-7.2 s from 09:00Z - roughly 1.3 s worse than order-service and starting in the same bucket (08:56Z).

ledger-db itself degraded at the same 08:56Z bucket: slow_queries_per_min jumped from ~0.77-1.61 baseline to avg 70.42 (max 139.68) at 08:56Z and ~135-148/min thereafter; simultaneously connections_active rose from ~60-64 to avg 127.45 (max 199.81) at 08:56Z and ~185-204 after 09:00Z. So the DB-level symptom predates the order-service ERROR logs by ~4 minutes.

order-service db_pool_in_use saturated concurrently: flat ~13.5-14.4 connections through 08:52Z, then avg 21.72 (max 45.07) at 08:56Z and pinned at ~44-48 (max 51.63) from 09:00Z - consistent with pooled connections held open by blocked INSERT INTO orders statements rather than a pool leak before 08:56Z.

events.answer: Onset is in the 08:52-08:56Z bucket (240s granularity) on 2026-05-05, ~14-18 min before the 09:10Z report: ledger-db slow_queries_per_min jumped from ~1/min to 70.42/min and connections_active from ~62 to 127.45, while both order-service p99 (150 ms -> 1515 ms, then ~5.2 s) and portfolio-service p99 (180 ms -> 3574 ms, then ~7.0 s) broke at the same 08:56Z bucket. The symptom is NOT order-service-specific: ledger-db's slow queries are all Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907) attributed to application_name=portfolio-service (first at 08:58:38Z), and portfolio-service is degraded more than order-service; order-service's first statement-timeout error is at 09:00:42Z (284 total, 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)', continuing to 10:58Z). Earliest error signature in the window is the ledger-db slow-query Seq Scan at 08:58:38Z, i.e. DB-layer contention precedes the client-facing order-service errors.

events.statement: Only two changes exist in the entire 2026-05-04..2026-05-05 window: cfg-2903 on ledger-db (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1 at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z, author dba-team) and dep-5905 on portfolio-service (v4.5.0 at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z, author k.shah, 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at', 'no migration included', status 'live', rolled_back_at null). Both predate the 09:10Z report; ordering alone does not discriminate, so timing match to the 08:52-08:56Z onset must.

The autovacuum change timing does NOT match the degradation: cfg-2903 was applied at 08:00:00Z, and a ledger-db-only re-query confirms it is the sole change and nothing else was applied to ledger-db after 08:00Z up to 08:55Z. Per T1/F11, ledger-db stayed at baseline (~0.77-1.61 slow_queries_per_min, ~60-64 connections_active) through 08:52Z and only broke at the 08:56Z bucket (~70.42/min, ~127 connections) - a ~52-minute gap between change and any measurable DB effect.

The portfolio-service deployment and the symptom onset coincide: dep-5905 deployed 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z carries a 'new query on trades' with no index/migration; ledger-db's slow-query WARNs (all 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)', application_name=portfolio-service, first at 08:58:38Z) and the p99 inflection for both order-service (08:56Z bucket -> ~1515ms then ~5.2s) and portfolio-service (08:56Z bucket -> ~3574ms then ~7.0s) all fall within the same 08:52-08:56Z window.

The shared-component chain explains cross-service impact and predicts which callers are hit. ledger-db ('shared':true, type postgres) is a direct 'db' dependency of order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service, and order-service reaches it directly (no ledger-service in the graph). So DB contention from one caller propagates to all four; the observed pattern (portfolio-service worst at ~7.0s, order-service ~5.2s, both starting in the same 08:56Z bucket) matches a shared-DB cause rather than an order-service-local fault.

Historical precedent directly matches the supported theory (leads only, not evidence for this incident): HIST-111 (2025-05-22) 'Reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db', services [ledger-db, settlement-service], root_cause 'New report query without index did sequential scans', category 'bad_deployment' - i.e. an un-indexed report query causing Seq Scans on ledger-db, the same signature seen now. The other incident mentioning autovacuum was not retrievable (last search hit the tool-call budget).

Failure signature is a DB statement timeout propagated to the client layer, not an order-service fault: order-service's only ERROR pattern is 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' (first 09:00:42Z, 284 total to 10:58Z), i.e. order-service is a victim of ledger-db write contention, while the originating load is portfolio-service's trade Seq Scans. payment-service and settlement-service share the same ledger-db edge and would be expected to degrade similarly.

events.answer: The evidence supports the PORTFOLIO-SERVICE v4.5.0 DEPLOYMENT (dep-5905, 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z, adding a new un-indexed query on trades) as the temporally and causally plausible trigger, NOT the autovacuum change. The autovacuum change (cfg-2903) at 08:00:00Z precedes onset by ~52 min but is temporally disconnected: ledger-db metrics stayed at baseline (~0.77-1.61 slow queries/min, ~60 connections) through 08:52Z and only degraded at the same 08:56Z bucket as the deploy. The deploy, the DB degradation, both services' latency inflection and the portfolio-service Seq Scan all land in the 08:52-08:56Z window (with the Seq Scan WARN at 08:58:38Z), so the deploy is the change that temporally matches the degradation. The shared-component chain explains crossing-service impact: ledger-db is shared by four services, and the dominant symptom is a Seq Scan on trades attributed to portfolio-service, with portfolio-service degraded worse (~7.0s) than order-service (~5.2s) - consistent with a query-driven DB contention propagated to all callers rather than an order-service-specific fault.
